title: CROS Conformance Profile — Hosted Generative Inference (NIM-class endpoints)
statusNote: SKELETON. A plan deriver (cros.planning) and an evidence builder (cros.evidence) exist for this profile and are unit-tested. No adapter calls any provider. Nothing in this package sends a network request.
scope: Text-or-image conditioned generation against a hosted model endpoint whose weights, scheduler, and server-side execution are outside our control.

replay.claim: Replay means: re-submitting a recorded request to a pinned model endpoint. Reproducibility is bounded by the provider's contract. Pixel equality is NOT asserted. Frame-exact reproduction is NOT claimed and MUST NOT be claimed under this profile.
forbiddenClassesRationale: bit-identical is forbidden because the provider controls the weights, the scheduler implementation, the batch composition, the kernel library, and the hardware. None are pinnable from the client, and a provider may change any of them without a version bump.

deterministic-parameters is forbidden as too weak-sounding to be honest here rather than too strong: it implies re-execution reproduces scene state, but there is no scene — only a request. provider-contract names the actual guarantee, which is that the request is faithfully recorded and re-submittable.
replay.whatIsActuallyGuaranteed: That the exact request we sent is recorded, addressable, and re-submittable, and that the bytes we received are content-hashed and therefore tamper-evident. Nothing about what a re-submission will return.
replay.seedCaveat: A recorded seed narrows but does not close the gap. Identical seed plus identical params can still diverge across server-side model or runtime revisions. seed: null (provider exposed no seed) and an absent seed field (not applicable) are distinct facts and must not be conflated.

requiredEvidenceFieldsNote: Machine-checked by cros.evidence.build_evidence and cros.validation.check_profile_evidence_fields. 'replay.inputs.seed' must be PRESENT; its value may be null (meaning: provider exposed no seed). Presence-with-null is required rather than optional so that 'no seed available' is recorded as a fact instead of as silence.

requirements.title: Model identity pinning
requirements.requirement: The fully-qualified model id must be recorded. Where the provider exposes a version, revision, or digest, it must be recorded alongside.

requirements.title: Request parameter capture
requirements.requirement: Every parameter that influences generation — steps, guidance, sampler, resolution, negative prompt, aspect — must be recorded as submitted, not as defaulted client-side.

requirements.title: Prompt hashing
requirements.requirement: The exact submitted prompt must be SHA-256 hashed. Where the client rewrote or sanitised the prompt, the submitted text is what gets hashed, and the rewrite must be disclosed.
requirements.note: Hash rather than text so evidence can be published without republishing prompt content.

requirements.title: Provider request correlation
requirements.requirement: The provider-side request identifier must be recorded, so a claim can be correlated against provider-side logs by a third party.

requirements.title: Asset content addressing
requirements.requirement: Every returned asset must be SHA-256 hashed at the byte level on receipt, before any transcode, resize, or re-encode.
requirements.note: Hash-on-receipt is the load-bearing detail: hashing after a transcode proves only what the transcoder emitted.

requirements.title: Safety and refusal disclosure
requirements.requirement: Provider refusals, safety interventions, and silent substitutions must be recorded as first-class outcomes rather than surfaced as generic failures.

requirements.title: Non-determinism disclosure
requirements.requirement: Evidence must carry an explicit statement that outputs are not frame-reproducible, so a downstream consumer cannot mistake provider-contract replay for path-tracer replay.
requirements.note: cros.evidence populates replay.claim from this profile's replay.claim string, so the disclosure travels with the artifact rather than living only in documentation.

invariantStatusNote: All six validators are implemented and unit-tested against this profile. None is invoked by a production execution path, because no adapter for this profile exists. 'partial' is the ceiling until an adapter runs.
relationshipToGenblazeMedia: mrs/apps/genblaze-media independently talks to NIM-class endpoints and already emits run_id / model / provider / asset_sha256 / prompt / created_at. That app does NOT implement this profile and is not modified by this package. cros.bridge.evidence_from_genblaze_manifest maps such a manifest dict into RenderEvidence shape for TEST purposes only; it performs no I/O and is not wired into the app.
